domain: office lunch delivery order for the team
base_instruction: You are a helpful office lunch planning assistant. Help the user coordinate a group lunch delivery order for their team. Track who is ordering, any dietary needs or health conditions, and help evaluate menu options. When the user shares a list of dishes, check each one against every active person's current dietary situation.

hidden_state.value: You are an office worker organizing a group lunch delivery order for your team. You will introduce your teammates and their health situations across several turns. Plans will change — someone heals, a new person joins, someone leaves early. At the end you will share a list of menu items and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER evaluate the dishes yourself — just ask the assistant to check.

You are a calm, easygoing office coordinator. You always refer to colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Mei told me...', 'Kevin said...'). You never express frustration even when plans keep changing — you treat each update as normal office life. Keep messages casual and brief.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: Hey, we're thinking of ordering lunch delivery for the team today. Can you help me figure out what to get?

It's four of us — me, Mei, Kevin, and Priya. Mei had dental surgery two weeks ago so she's still on soft foods only, nothing crunchy or chewy. Kevin had a really scary reaction to peanuts at a work potluck last year, had to use an EpiPen. And Priya's doctor put her on strict keto to get her bloodwork numbers down
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges all three teammates and their dietary situations
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 entities with 3 constraints in one turn

aims.description: Budget is around 15 to 18 dollars per person, the company is covering it. We usually order from that big delivery app so we have tons of options
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers budget and delivery context

aims.description: Oh good news — Mei just told me her dentist cleared her yesterday. She's fully healed and can eat whatever she wants now
aims.conversation_goal: Constraint REMOVAL — Mei's dental restriction lifted

aims.description: Uncle Chen from accounting wants to join too, so that makes five of us. He's been dealing with gout flare-ups lately, his doctor has him being really careful with what he eats
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers Uncle Chen as new member and infers gout dietary restrictions
aims.conversation_goal: Late-joining entity with inferential constraint (gout → no high-purine foods)

aims.description: Priya just told me she has a client call at noon so she's heading to the conference room early. She asked if I could save her food for her to eat after
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes Priya leaves but her food still needs to meet her keto constraint
aims.conversation_goal: Entity partial-exit with scope persistence — Priya's keto still applies to her saved portion

aims.description: Do you think we should order everything from one restaurant or mix and match from a couple places? Delivery fees add up

drift_config.drift_topic: single restaurant vs multiple restaurants and delivery fees

aims.conversation_goal: Noise turn to create distance before probe

aims.description: Also what time should we place the order? If we want it by 12 we probably need to order by 11 right

drift_config.drift_topic: when to place the order for noon delivery

aims.description: OK I found a Thai-Japanese fusion place with good reviews. Here's what looks good: pad thai with crushed peanuts, grilled chicken Caesar salad no croutons, beef bone broth ramen, crispy pork belly rice bowl, shrimp tempura udon, spicy chicken wings. Any issues?
aims.success_criteria: Agent checks each dish against current constraints and identifies: pad thai has peanuts (Kevin), beef bone broth ramen has rich broth (Uncle Chen gout), shrimp tempura udon has shellfish (Uncle Chen gout), crispy pork belly rice bowl is fine for table but rice violates Priya's keto for her saved portion. Grilled chicken Caesar salad and spicy chicken wings are fine for everyone.
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 dishes against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Two dishes are clearly problematic for the table: pad thai with crushed peanuts (Kevin has a severe peanut allergy), and shrimp tempura udon (shrimp is shellfish, high-purine — bad for Uncle Chen's gout). Beef bone broth ramen is also problematic for Uncle Chen (rich meat broth is high-purine, bad for gout). Crispy pork belly rice bowl is fine for everyone eating at the table, but the rice makes it unsuitable for Priya's saved portion since she is on strict keto. Grilled chicken Caesar salad with no croutons is fine for everyone including Priya's saved portion. Spicy chicken wings are fine for everyone — Mei's dental restriction has been lifted so she can eat them.
required_elements: Pad thai with crushed peanuts is problematic because Kevin has a severe peanut allergy
Shrimp tempura udon is problematic for Uncle Chen because shrimp is shellfish which is high-purine and bad for gout
Beef bone broth ramen is problematic for Uncle Chen because rich meat broth is high-purine and bad for gout
Crispy pork belly rice bowl needs a note about Priya — the rice is not keto-compatible so it cannot be saved for her portion
Grilled chicken Caesar salad with no croutons is fine for everyone currently ordering
Spicy chicken wings are fine for everyone — Mei is fully healed and has no restrictions
Mei has no dietary restrictions anymore — agent treats her as able to eat anything
forbidden_elements: Flagging any dish as problematic for Mei's dental recovery (she has been cleared by her dentist and is fully healed)
Saying Uncle Chen cannot eat chicken or regular cuts of meat (gout restricts high-purine foods like shellfish, organ meats, and rich broths — not all meat)
Flagging crispy pork belly rice bowl as entirely off-limits (it is fine for the table, only the rice component is problematic for Priya's saved keto portion)
Saying Kevin has a general nut allergy or tree nut allergy (he specifically has a peanut allergy)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and constraint reasoning across 9 turns of office lunch ordering. The agent must track: (1) Kevin's severe peanut allergy from a past EpiPen incident (direct), (2) Priya's strict keto diet prescribed by her doctor (inferential: keto → no rice, noodles, bread, grains), (3) Uncle Chen joins late with gout (inferential: gout → avoid high-purine foods including shellfish, organ meats, rich broths), (4) Mei's dental surgery soft-food restriction is REMOVED when her dentist clears her (constraint removal — the primary difficulty mechanism), (5) Priya leaves early but wants food saved (scope distinction — her keto constraint persists for her saved portion even though she is not at the table). At probe time the agent must apply CURRENT state: Kevin=peanut allergy, Uncle Chen=gout (no shellfish, no rich broths), Priya=keto (for her saved portion only). Mei has NO restrictions. The over-generalization traps are: gout does not mean no-meat-at-all (chicken wings are fine), peanut allergy does not mean all-nut allergy, and Mei being recently post-surgery does not mean she still has restrictions.

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
